You have an opportunity to use the most effective teaching tactics, ones that public schools cant use.

Teach your kids how to self-teach: The most effective way to learn is to alternate study with practice, slowly shifting from primarily study to primarily practice. If you want to learn to golf, read the rules and go golf. Now come back and learn the strategy, how to swing, etc. Go play again. Now stop and just think about any aspect that you're having trouble with, such as putting, now do a focused practice on just that aspect. Then go play more. Repeat as needed. In a few weeks you'll become a very good golfer. This strategy can be used for everything. When you master this skill, its easy to learn any new skill.

Learn by teaching: The best way know if you really understand something is if you can teach it. Have your wife teach your kids to do algebra, then have them teach you how to do it. Tell them to read up on the American revolution and teach you what happened. For abstract things like philosophy the best way to explain something is the 1-3-1 format. You start with a summary 2-3 paragraphs. Then you explain it in three different ways, each several pages, ELI5, using different examples and different supporting data. Finally you summarize what you explained, maybe 3 or 4 paragraphs. When you master this skill you can teach even the most complex subject matter to anyone.

Critical thinking: Show them how to figure things out for themselves. Ask them leading questions or give hints if they're way off base. Be willing to let them try their plan and ask why they failed or what they could do better. This also teaches leadership. "Son, we have to change the oil on the car. What tools should I get? What should we do first?" When discussing things like history have them take all major sides and explain the motivations and goals of each.

Encourage their first jobs to be ones that involve sales and negotiation. Even if it means selling candy bars door to door.
